lines.text: Apollo Thirteen's oxygen tank was already dangerous on the launch pad.
lines.headline:
Doomed
on the pad

lines.text: During ground tests, its heaters were powered from a sixty-five volt supply.
But its thermostatic switches were rated for twenty-eight volts.
They were meant to open at eighty degrees, and at sixty-five volts they could not.
The heater tube may have reached a thousand degrees, damaging the insulation on the fan wires.
In flight, the crew switched on the tank's fans, and about ninety seconds later the tank lost pressure.
The board found an electrically initiated fire inside oxygen tank number two.
It was a near disaster, averted only by the crew and the ground control team.
The flight was saved in space. The tank was lost on the ground.
